## Tier

<!--
1 = Major site (Stonehenge, Giza, Machu Picchu — global recognition)
2 = Significant site (substantial coverage in alt-archaeology, UNESCO usually)
3 = Specialist interest (real but lesser-known)
-->

## Description

<!--
2-4 sentences in the atlas's editorial voice. Factual, evocative, no fluff.

Style notes :
- No em dashes (use periods, commas, colons)
- No "genuinely", "delve", "straightforward"
- Future-forward language, specificity over negation
- Tier-1 sites can be more declarative; tier-3 sites stay measured
-->

Description :

## Why this site belongs in the atlas

<!--
Editorial reasoning. The atlas catalogs significant, ancient, well-documented sites.

Examples of strong cases :
- "Newly significant archaeology since 2020; multiple researchers have called for renewed attention."
- "Visually unique stone-cut form not represented elsewhere in the catalog."
- "Cluster of related sites in this region warrants a representative entry."

Examples of weaker cases :
- "I think it's cool."
- "It has 200 reviews on TripAdvisor."
-->
